static_findings.snippet: - Call `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__list_sims` and select the simulator with state `Booted`.
- If the app is already built and only launch is requested, use `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__launch_app_sim`
- **Tap**: `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__tap` (prefer `id` or `label`; use coordinates only if needed).
- **Gestures**: `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__gesture` for common scrolls and edge swipes.
- Start logs: `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__start_sim_log_cap` with the app bundle id.
- Stop logs: `mcp__XcodeBuildMCP__stop_sim_log_cap` and summarize important lines.
- For console output, set `captureConsole: true` and relaunch if required.
- If build fails, ask whether to retry with `preferXcodebuild: true`.
- If UI elements are not hittable, re-run `describe_ui` after layout changes.

content.user_title: Debug iOS Apps in the Simulator
content.value_statement: iOS simulator debugging often requires several build, launch, UI, and log steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through XcodeBuildMCP workflows for focused app diagnosis.
actual_capabilities: Lists booted iOS simulators through XcodeBuildMCP before choosing a target device.
Sets project, workspace, scheme, simulator, and debug configuration defaults for a session.
Builds and runs the current app on a simulator when the user requests it.
Launches an already built app and resolves bundle identifiers when needed.
Describes simulator UI state, taps controls, types text, performs gestures, and captures screenshots.
Starts and stops simulator log capture, then summarizes relevant console output.
limitations: Requires XcodeBuildMCP tools, Xcode, and a valid iOS project in the current workspace.
Requires a booted simulator unless the user explicitly asks to boot one.
Depends on correct project, workspace, scheme, and bundle identifier information.
Screenshots and logs can contain sensitive app data and should be handled carefully.

use_cases.title: Run a Local iOS Build
use_cases.description: Build and launch the current app on a booted simulator, then report build or runtime problems.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Simulator Screen
use_cases.description: Describe visible UI elements and verify whether a screen matches the expected app state.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Runtime Behavior
use_cases.description: Capture simulator logs and summarize errors, warnings, or console output linked to a user action.

prompt_templates.title: Run the App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the iOS debugger agent to find the booted simulator, set session defaults, build, and run this app.

prompt_templates.title: Check the Current Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the iOS debugger agent to inspect the running simulator UI and summarize what is visible on screen.

prompt_templates.title: Reproduce a UI Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the iOS debugger agent to launch the app, describe the UI, tap the relevant controls, and report where the flow fails.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Logs and Bundle State
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the iOS debugger agent to confirm the bundle identifier, relaunch with console capture, reproduce the issue, and summarize important log lines.

output_examples.input: Run the iOS app on the booted simulator and tell me if it starts.
output_examples.output: The app built successfully and launched on the booted simulator. The first screen is visible, and no startup errors appeared in the captured console output.

output_examples.input: Inspect the current simulator screen after tapping Sign In.
output_examples.output: The simulator shows a sign-in form with email and password fields. The Sign In button remains disabled until both fields contain text.

output_examples.input: Capture logs while I reproduce the crash.
output_examples.output: Log capture started, the action was reproduced, and the relevant output points to a view model error during data loading.

best_practices: Confirm the booted simulator and scheme before running build or launch actions.
Use UI description before taps, typing, or gestures to avoid unintended simulator actions.
Summarize only relevant logs and avoid sharing sensitive screen or console data.
anti_patterns: Do not run simulator actions without a clear user request or debugging goal.
Do not assume a bundle identifier when XcodeBuildMCP can resolve it from the app path.
Do not paste full logs when a concise error summary is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps build, launch, inspect, and debug an iOS app on a booted simulator using XcodeBuildMCP.

faq.question: Does it require XcodeBuildMCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on XcodeBuildMCP tools for simulator control, UI inspection, and log capture.

faq.question: Can it boot a simulator automatically?
faq.answer: It asks the user to boot a simulator unless the user explicitly requests simulator booting.

faq.question: Can it interact with the app UI?
faq.answer: Yes. It can describe the UI, tap controls, type text, perform gestures, and capture screenshots.

faq.question: Can it diagnose console output?
faq.answer: Yes. It can start and stop simulator log capture, then summarize important runtime messages.

faq.question: What information should users protect?
faq.answer: Users should review screenshots and logs because they may include account data, test records, or private app content.
